name: Zuo Zongshen
current_role: Founder & chairman, Zongshen Industrial Group; chairman, Chongqing Zongshen Power Machinery (SZSE: 001696), re-elected Sept 2025
profile: Chongqing-born entrepreneur (b. 1952) who turned a 1982 motorcycle repair shed known as 'Master Zuo' into Zongshen Industrial Group, a major Chinese motorcycle and engine maker with 20,000+ staff. In September 2025 he was re-appointed chairman of the listed Zongshen Power Machinery board.
interesting_fact: He learned motorcycle repair working under his brother-in-law, opened his own shop in 1982 in a street-front room in Banan, Chongqing, and in 1992 borrowed 300,000 yuan to register Chongqing Zongshen Motorcycle Technology Development Co., the start of the group.
deep_cut_fact: Before the repair shop, after quitting his 'iron rice bowl' job as a kiln worker at a Chongqing porcelain factory in the early 1980s, he tried peddling martial-arts (wuxia) novels in Hebei and then fruit and clothing in Shandong, without success.
notes: No personal contacts published. Formal route is the IR/securities office of listed subsidiary Chongqing Zongshen Power Machinery (SZSE 001696; board secretary Lin Yi). Daughter Zuo Ying is described as successor running group investments.

name: Wu Po Sum
current_role: Chairman & non-executive director, Central China Management Co. (HKEX: 9982); founder and director of Central China Real Estate (HKEX: 832)
profile: Wu Po Sum (Mandarin: Hu Baosen), b. ~1950 in Henan, founded Jianye/Central China Real Estate in Zhengzhou in 1992 after a decade in Hong Kong trade, building it into Henan's leading developer. He chairs asset-light spin-off Central China Management, holding 47.59% via Joy Bright Investments (end-2025), and controls insurer Central China New Life.
interesting_fact: Known as Henan's 'godfather of football': in 1994 he founded Henan Jianye FC, which kept the same name from the start of China's professional league until a 2021 rule change, and he vowed to fund Henan football 'until Jianye goes bankrupt'.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in English from Zhengzhou University in 1979, he joined the Henan branch of China Textiles Import & Export Corp., which sent him to Hong Kong in 1982 to set up a trading company - a decade of export work before he returned home to found Jianye.
notes: Usually reported in Chinese as Hu Baosen (胡葆森). Contacts are company IR (Central China Management), not personal. Group has been in debt restructuring since 2022-23; avoid the topic in outreach.

name: Zhang Jindong
current_role: Founder and honorary chairman, Suning.com (stepped down as chairman July 2021); chairman of private parent Suning Holdings Group
profile: Nanjing literature graduate (b. 1963, Tianchang, Anhui) who opened a single air-conditioner shop in Nanjing in December 1990 and built Suning into one of China's largest appliance and e-commerce retailers, later buying 70% of Inter Milan (2016). After a 2021 state-led bailout he became honorary chairman; reports in 2024 said he was again steering the retailer's turnaround.
interesting_fact: He started Suning on 26 Dec 1990 with 100,000 yuan of his own money, renting a 200 sq m storefront on Ninghai Road, Nanjing, that sold only air conditioners.
deep_cut_fact: Because the first shop opened in winter, he pushed the units' heating mode with the slogan 'Buy a heating air conditioner and have a cozy New Year' (买一台取暖空调，舒舒服服过个年). Before that he had worked at the Gulou District Industrial Company after studying Chinese at Nanjing Normal University (1984).
notes: Lost control of Suning.com in the 2021 bailout (Suning's finances and Inter Milan sale are sensitive; avoid). Contacts are Suning.com's securities/IR office, not personal. Brother Zhang Guiping (Suning Universal) is a separate billionaire.

profile: Hurun China lists Zhou Jun (周骏) with wealth from Ganten, the Shenzhen bottled-water group founded in 1992 that owns the Ganten purified-water and Baisuishan (100 Mountain) mineral-water brands, exported to 30+ countries. No independent biography of Zhou Jun or confirmation of his role could be found in this pass.
interesting_fact: Ganten's Baisuishan brand markets itself as 'the aristocrat of water' (水中贵族) and runs a series of high-production costume-drama style TV ads; the company says its water is exported to more than 30 countries and regions.

name: Xiong Yonghong
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Anhui Sinomag Technology Co. (Longci Keji, SZSE: 300835)
profile: Co-founded the predecessor of Sinomag in Hefei in 1998 (renamed Anhui Longci/Sinomag in 2001), which grew into a top global maker of wet-pressed permanent-ferrite magnet tiles used in car, motorcycle, power-tool and appliance motors. Listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020; he debuted on the Hurun China list in 2026 as the company expands in Vietnam and into chip inductors.
interesting_fact: Sinomag has a manufacturing subsidiary in Vietnam (Vietnam Longci), and a 2026 share placement of up to 760m yuan is funding a second Vietnam phase adding 10,000 t of ferrite magnet-tile capacity, plus a chip-inductor project.
deep_cut_fact: He came from trade, not engineering: with a technical-secondary-school education, he worked as a business manager in the documents/storage department and then 'Export Department No. 8' of Anhui Import & Export (Group) Corp. before running magnet ventures and founding Sinomag.
notes: Hurun lists wealth source as 'Sinomag' (龙磁科技). Formal route is the company's board-secretary/IR office via SZSE cninfo disclosures; official site sinomag.com.cn did not load during research.

name: Sukhpal Singh Ahluwalia
current_role: Founder and non-executive chairman, Dominvs Group (London real estate, hotels and asset management)
profile: Kampala-born (1958) British entrepreneur whose family fled Idi Amin's Uganda in 1972. He founded Euro Car Parts in 1978 and grew it to 3,500 staff and 89 sites before selling it to LKQ in 2011 for GBP 280m plus earn-out; he chaired LKQ's UK/Ireland/India arm until 2018 and now runs Dominvs Group, a family hotel and property business.
interesting_fact: He arrived in the UK as a 13-year-old refugee, and the family spent its first year in temporary shared accommodation; he later built Euro Car Parts from a single shop bought with GBP 5,000.
deep_cut_fact: Euro Car Parts began as a Willesden shop called 'Highway Autos', bought with GBP 5,000 borrowed from his father plus a bank loan; it was renamed a year later and first specialised in BMW, Mercedes, Porsche and VW parts. As a teenager he had spent time trading around Petticoat Lane market.
notes: Won Business Person of the Year at the 2024 Asian Achievers Awards. Dominvs Group's site (dominvsgroup.com) blocked automated access, so no published contact was verified; corporate contact page there is the likely route. Wikipedia article carries an 'undisclosed paid editing' tag - double-check details.

name: Shan Yigang
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, KE Holdings (Beike; NYSE: BEKE, HKEX: 2423)
profile: Shan Yigang (b. ~1972) co-founded Beike, China's largest housing-transaction and services platform, with Zuo Hui and Peng Yongdong, after joining Lianjia's board in 2007. He remains an executive director of KE Holdings, a director of rental platform Ziroom since 2017, and an independent director of fitness app Keep (HKEX: 3650) since 2023.
interesting_fact: He sits on the board of Keep, the Chinese fitness app, as an independent non-executive director - an unusual side role for a property-tech founder.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lianjia/Beike he was a co-founder and vice president of Dalian Haowangjiao Real Estate Brokerage (Dec 1999 - Nov 2007), a regional agency in Dalian; he later completed a Tsinghua EMBA in 2019.
notes: Low personal media profile; route via KE Holdings IR (ir@ke.com). Age 53 per FY2025 20-F.

name: Ma Bingbing
current_role: Chairwoman and legal representative, Zhongzhong Science & Technology (Tianjin) Co. (SSE: 603135)
profile: Ma Bingbing (46, per the 2025 annual report) is chairwoman and co-controlling shareholder, with vice-chair Gu Fenglan, of Zhongzhong Science & Technology, a Tianjin maker of specialised steel-rolling and metallurgical equipment listed in Shanghai in 2023. She served as a supervisor of the predecessor engineering firm from 2001, became its chair in 2020 and the listed company's chair in 2021.
interesting_fact: Her involvement predates the listed group: she has been a supervisor of affiliate Tianjin Tianzhong Zhongzhi Science & Technology Engineering since May 1998, and now heads a group whose subsidiaries span hydraulics, continuous casting and intelligent electrics in Tianjin and Jiangsu.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2025 the metallurgy-equipment maker moved into robotics, setting up Zhongzhong Lingxi Robot Technology (Jiangsu) with a Shanghai branch to build industrial/collaborative-robot flexible production lines and special-purpose robots; Ma sits on its board.
notes: Female (input has no country; company is in Tianjin, China). Shares control with Gu Fenglan (75). Revenue fell sharply in 2025 per annual report - avoid. Contacts are company IR.

name: Liu Daojun
current_role: No current public role found; former director (2004-2022) and co-founding shareholder of Jiangxi Zhengbang Technology (SZSE: 002157)
profile: Liu Daojun (legal name Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun, Canadian national, b. Oct 1972) co-founded the listed Zhengbang Technology with Lin Yinsun's Zhengbang Group, a Jiangxi feed and hog-farming giant, and sat on its board from 2004 to 2022 as a large non-controlling shareholder (169.6m shares at end-2019). Zhengbang has since been restructured under new control; his current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: Though listed by Hurun as a Chinese billionaire, filings identify him as a Canadian citizen named Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun - unrelated to Zhengbang's controlling family, yet a founding promoter of the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before and alongside Zhengbang he chaired Jiangxi Zhengbang Industrial, Yunnan Guanglian Livestock & Poultry and Nanchang Guanglian Industrial, and took no pay from the listed company as a director.
notes: Left Zhengbang board in 2022; the company went through court restructuring in 2023 and is now controlled by the Twins Group - avoid that topic. No personal channels found. Very low profile.

name: Leslie Jeannine Rainbolt
current_role: Director (since 2023) and ~14.6% beneficial owner, BancFirst Corp. (NASDAQ: BANF), Oklahoma City; private investor
profile: Dr. Leslie J. Rainbolt (68) is a pediatric dermatologist and private investor from the Oklahoma family behind BancFirst; she is the sister of chairman David E. Rainbolt. She is managing partner of Main Street Banking Partners LP, which holds 4.91m BancFirst shares (her beneficial stake: 14.64%), and joined the bank's board in 2023.
interesting_fact: A physician-banker: she earned her M.D. at the University of Oklahoma, joined OU Health Sciences Center's dermatology faculty in 1994 teaching and practising pediatric dermatology, and also holds an MBA from Thunderbird School of Global Management.
deep_cut_fact: She served 14 years (2006-2020) on the University of Oklahoma Board of Regents, and kept teaching at OU as a volunteer faculty member after leaving full-time practice.
notes: Proxy lists her contact for shareholder purposes as BancFirst's corporate P.O. Box 26788, Oklahoma City, OK 73126 (company mailing address). Brother David E. Rainbolt chairs BancFirst. Low media profile; formal route via BancFirst corporate secretary.

name: Kristina Burow
current_role: Managing Director, ARCH Venture Partners (San Diego); director of Scholar Rock, Kardigan and Neumora (co-founder), among others
profile: Biotech venture capitalist (53) who joined ARCH Venture Partners in 2002 as an associate and became a managing director, co-founding or backing companies such as Receptos (sold to Celgene), Vividion (Bayer), Orbital (BMS), Metsera (Pfizer) and Neumora. Trained as a chemist, she earlier ran chemistry operations at the Genomics Institute of the Novartis Research Foundation.
interesting_fact: She has co-founded four biotechs that were acquired by big pharma - Receptos (Celgene), Vividion (Bayer), Orbital Therapeutics (Bristol Myers Squibb) and Metsera (Pfizer).
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital she was an early employee at the Genomics Institute of the Novartis Research Foundation (GNF) in San Diego, directing chemistry operations and helping spin companies out of GNF; she holds a B.S. in chemistry from UC Berkeley and an M.A. in chemistry from Columbia.
notes: The ~$500m 'SEC insider holdings' figure almost certainly reflects ARCH fund stakes she is attributed as an insider/10% owner, not personal wealth. Route via ARCH Venture Partners (archventure.com blocked automated access; contact page not verified).
